Near Cache

1. What is a Near Cache?
  • A near cache is a local, on-heap cache of the most recently or frequently accessed entries from a distributed cache;
  • It sits on the client node (or any node) and serves reads locally, avoiding network hops;
  • Particularly useful for PARTITIONED caches where reads may require contacting remote nodes;
2. How does it work?
  • When you read a key, the result is cached locally in the near cache;
  • Subsequent reads for the same key are served from the local near cache — no network hop;
  • When the entry is updated on the primary node, all near caches that hold that entry are automatically invalidated;
  • The near cache is populated on-demand (read-through), not preloaded;
3. Configuring Near Cache
  • On the server (cache configuration): 
    NearCacheConfiguration<Integer, String> nearCfg = new NearCacheConfiguration<>();
nearCfg.setNearEvictionPolicy(new LruEvictionPolicy<>(100_000));

CacheConfiguration<Integer, String> cacheCfg = new CacheConfiguration<>("myCache");
cacheCfg.setNearConfiguration(nearCfg);

ignite.createCache(cacheCfg);
  • On a client node (at runtime): 
    NearCacheConfiguration<Integer, String> nearCfg = new NearCacheConfiguration<>();
nearCfg.setNearEvictionPolicy(new LruEvictionPolicy<>(50_000));

IgniteCache<Integer, String> cache = ignite.createNearCache("myCache", nearCfg);
4. Eviction Policies for Near Cache
PolicyDescription
LruEvictionPolicyRemoves least recently used entries when max size is reached
FifoEvictionPolicyRemoves oldest entries (first in, first out)
SortedEvictionPolicyRemoves entries based on custom comparator
5. When to use Near Cache
  • When you have a read-heavy workload with a hot set of frequently accessed keys;
  • When reads from client nodes are latency-sensitive and the data is in PARTITIONED mode;
  • Avoid near cache for write-heavy workloads — frequent invalidations negate the benefit;
